Description

Within minutes of stimulation ERK turns back on the receptor complex that started its activation. ERK phosphorylates human SOS1 on several serines in its C-terminal tail, near the proline-rich sites that bind GRB2, and SOS1 without these sites binds GRB2 more tightly [1, 2]. What follows depends on the receptor. With insulin, the phosphorylation releases SOS1 from GRB2 and so ends the activation of RAS [3, 4]. With EGF, SOS1 bound through GRB2 to the receptor at the plasma membrane is not uncoupled from GRB2. EGF instead releases the GRB2:SOS1 pair from the adaptor SHC [5]. A second kinase acts on the same tail. RSK, itself activated by ERK, phosphorylates SOS1 on Ser1134 and Ser1161, which creates binding sites for 14-3-3 proteins, Ser1134 being the main one, and modestly increases and prolongs the activation of ERK when it is prevented [2, 6].
